| [CLAIM-290](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-290.md) | A positive-definite kernel's minimal realizations are unique up to a unitary, and two finite representation matrices with the same centred Gram matrix differ by a translation and an orthogonal map | The record's own proofs of two steps that [THEORY-004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md) rests on and that its sources state without proof. (b) The finite case that [LIT-250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-250.md) §5.3 states as known: XXᵀ = YYᵀ implies Y = XQ with Q orthogonal, with no assumption that the rows span R^d. | [CLAIM-291](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-291.md) | The adjoint of a square-integrable integral operator is the integral operator with the conjugate-transposed kernel | The record's own step, written down in [THEORY-009](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-009.md) and marked there as not the Riesz article's, which covers matrices and bounded operators only. For a kernel k in L²(μ⊗ν), the operator (Tf)(x) = ∫ k(x,y) f(y) dν(y) from L²(ν) to L²(μ) has adjoint (T*g)(y) = ∫ k̄(x,y) g(x) dμ(x), by Cauchy–Schwarz and Fubini. So T is self-adjoint, when μ = ν, exactly when k(x,y) = k̄(y,x) almost everywhere. It does not say where the symmetry of k comes from, which is [THEORY-009](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-009.md)'s question, and it is not claimed for kernels that are not square-integrable. | Active |
| [CLAIM-356](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-356.md) v3 | An objective that originates outside a learning system can become a goal of the training organization, through its causal role in selecting, stabilizing and reproducing the learned structure it rewards; exogenous origin does not disqualify a goal, but it does not show that the network governs or endorses the objective, and what is selected is performance on the updating distribution, not generalization | The owner's, U35 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, against A34's guardrail that "Loss minimization does not automatically mean the model has its own goals": the externally assigned objective "can motivate identification and persistence of learned features", so the training process can be described as "having endogenous goals". A35 granted it: "Yes, in a qualified but important sense", and weakened the generalization half, since selection is for performance on "the encounters and feedback distribution actually used for updating". It objects in part to [CLAIM-288](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-288.md): it grants that a modeller-fixed objective does not show self-constitution, and denies that exogenous origin bars a goal from becoming the training organization's own regulation. The sharp edge: the goal belongs to the training organization ([CLAIM-367](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-367.md)), not to the network, and nothing here says the network endorses or governs it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-360](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-360.md) v2 | The deep-versus-shallow learning results separate three effects that aggregate loss conflates: a larger realizable function class, a larger set reachable within a fixed data and compute budget, and a different internal organization with the same attainable outcomes; the deep linear results show the third, the random-hierarchy results the second, and the depth-separation result for products of inputs the first, at fixed size | The owner's, U38 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, on A37's proposed experiment: "I think we may already have an empirical demonstration that would be useful here in the wide vs deep literature." | [CLAIM-366](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-366.md) v3 | Whether several objectives share a strict first-order descent direction, 0 ∉ conv{g_i}, is invariant under smooth invertible reparameterization, while the sign of a Euclidean gradient inner product is not, and a negative inner product does not exclude common descent; a budgeted version is invariant only with the metric pulled back | A35 §2 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, at the owner's U35 "double click" on whether functionally equivalent parameterizations give equivalent frustration diagnoses. Gradients transform as g′ = Jᵀg and directions as v′ = J⁻¹v, so directional derivatives, and with them the common-descent test 0 ∉ conv{g_i}, do not depend on coordinates. A Euclidean inner product does: g₁ = (1, 1), g₂ = (1, −½) have product ½, and under θ = diag(½, 2)ψ their transforms have −7/4, while d = (−1, 0) lowers both throughout. The sharp edge: it covers coordinate changes of one parameter space at first order, not function-preserving symmetries or training trajectories ([QUESTION-127](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-127.md)). The practice corollary, not to diagnose task conflict by gradient cosine, is the anthology's. | Active |
| [CLAIM-367](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-367.md) v4 | Whether a training-time regulatory condition belongs to a network depends on which unit is individuated for the training dynamics and whose jurisdiction governs the updates; in conventional training most of that governance falls to the optimizer–model–data system, so a condition of training is not thereby a condition of the network | The owner's correction, U31 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "it might help clarify things if we apply our individuation and volition frameworks to this system", the system being a deep network during training (U30). A31 granted it: "applying individuation first, then volition, then affect exposes a problem in our previous discussion". Individuated for the training dynamics, the unit is at least the network–optimizer pair; mapped through the six relations of will-organization, most of the governance of updates is outside the network's jurisdiction. So optimization difficulty in conventional training is real and belongs to the training system. The sharp edge: it does not say the governance is unreal, or that a network cannot come to hold some of it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-382](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-382.md) | In an autoencoder initialised with i.i.d. Gaussian weights and zero biases and trained by SGD or momentum SGD on a loss of its output, the law of each hidden layer's learned representation is invariant under every orthogonal map of that layer that commutes with its activation, so under a radial activation no basis is privileged in law, while elementwise tanh or Leaky-ReLU yields invariance only under the signed permutations or the permutations, which leaves the standard axes free to be privileged | [THEORY-288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-288.md)'s symmetry argument, stated as the record's own and proved. Transform the parameters by orthogonal maps Q_l of the hidden spaces that commute with the activation. The network then computes Q_l h_l and the same output, so the loss is invariant. Gradient steps commute with the transformation, and an i.i.d. Gaussian initialisation is invariant under it, so the law of the trained representations is too. For radial activations this is all of O(n), and no basis is privileged in law. For elementwise ones it is a finite group, so the axes may be privileged. Whether they are, and how strongly, is [THEORY-288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-288.md)'s empirical content. The argument needs an orthogonally equivariant optimiser, and fails for Adam. | Active |
| [CLAIM-387](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-387.md) | Optimal deterministic information-bottleneck partitions at two budgets need not be nested: with X uniform on four states and binary Y with P(Y=1\|x) = (0, 0, 1/8, 3/8), the optimum is {0,1,2 \| 3} for 6.91 < β < 9.26 and {0,1 \| 2,3} for 9.26 < β < 16.06, two partitions neither of which refines the other | Found by brute force in the reading of Equitz and Cover ([NOTE-988](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-988.md)) and re-run here from scratch. It answers the deterministic half of [QUESTION-220](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-220.md) in the negative: raising the budget can reorganize the optimal partition rather than split it. The two optima are not even laminar, so no fixed tree holds both as prunings, and [NOTE-676](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-676.md)'s nesting is bought by its tree restriction. It says nothing about stochastic encoders, where finite-β optima generally live ([THEORY-743](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-743.md)). | Active |
| [CLAIM-392](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-392.md) v2 | Stochastic information-bottleneck optima at two budgets need not be nested: for X uniform on four states and binary Y with P(Y=1\|x) = (0, 0, 1/8, 3/8), the unique optima at β = 8 and β = 12 admit no Markov chain X → T₂ → T₁, so raising the budget reorganizes the optimum even with noisy encoders | Computed in the reading of Charvin, Catenacci Volpi and Polani (2023), [NOTE-981](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-981.md), on the source of [CLAIM-387](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-387.md), and re-run here.
